title: OpenAI Halved My $200 Plan. So I Priced My Own AI Bill.

direction.name: Receipt Ledger Editorial (inherits ledger-editorial-v1)
direction.visual_spine: Porcelain field (#F6F4EF, the article charts' ground), graphite ink, serif claims, sans explanation, monospace receipt rows with dotted leaders that append and are never erased; one accent, receipt amber, reserved for cache reads / the re-read; tension by ink strike and stamp; charts appear only as framed exhibits with appending margin notes; the approved receipt cover bookends the film.

references.borrow: Append-only mono ledger rows, porcelain field, serif claims, header rail with appending chapter marker, phrase captions, one accent with one meaning, quiet brand end card.
references.avoid: Cyan/coral palette, the ink punctuation page, generated metaphor stills, and its 44/3 cascade as a stock effect.

references.borrow: The amber line item that runs off the receipt: reused as the film's one signature motion at the cache-read reveal.
references.avoid: Holding the cover full-frame behind narration beyond the opening and closing bookends.

references.borrow: Project-scoped composition with a Python data builder that derives scenes and captions from locked word timings.
references.avoid: Illustration-led field-note layouts; this film is typography- and evidence-led.

scenes.title: An agent doesn't answer once. It runs a loop.
scenes.purpose: Explains why cache reads dominate: every turn re-reads the conversation.
scenes.entry_visual: Five muted loop nodes scaffolded with the title visible at cut.
content: load repo context
call a tool
read the result
think
go again
every turn: re-read the conversation so far
cached re-reads are cheaper than fresh input
but the volume is enormous

beats.visual: Five muted loop nodes scaffolded with the title visible at cut.
amber return arc draws back to node 1

motion.continuity_anchor: Five loop nodes stay fixed; only the amber return path draws, arrowhead at p >= 0.98.
motion.why_not_static: The re-read is a return trip on every turn; drawing the path back to node 1 shows repetition, not a sixth step.
